reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is translating biomechanical data (hop distances) into actionable clinical predictions (RTS success). This necessitates a statistical learning framework that accounts for subject-specific heterogeneity and measurement noise. The hop test serves as a proxy for lower-limb power and symmetry, which are critical for dynamic sports activities. However, its predictive power is limited by the intrinsic variability in graft healing and neuromuscular adaptation. To mitigate this, we incorporate subgroup analyses (hamstring grafts, meniscal status) to identify patient strata where the test is most informative. The failure mode occurs when the test is applied outside its calibrated range (e.g., early post-op assessment), leading to spurious correlations. Thus, the primitive must be interpreted within the context of established biological timelines.
